# PyHP

> PHP syntax, Python brains, C muscles. PyHP is a dynamically typed scripting
> language with a PHP-family syntax (braces, semicolons, `echo`, `foreach`, no
> `$` before variables), Python semantics (aliasing lists/dicts, slicing with
> steps, comprehensions, lambdas & closures, classes with `super`, Python
> truthiness) and C muscles (hex/binary literals, bitwise operators, optional
> runtime-enforced static types, a malloc/free byte-buffer arena, file/env/exec
> access).

PyHP 0.2.0 runs on any PHP 8.0+ CLI with **two execution engines built from one
front-end**: a tree-walking interpreter (`pyhp run`, `pyhp repl`) and a
transpiler that emits standalone PHP 8 (`pyhp build`, `pyhp compile`). The
29-case test suite runs every program through both engines and requires
byte-identical output. Source of truth: https://github.com/Stevem100/pyhp

## Files in this folder (ai/)

- `pyhp-spec.json` — machine-readable language spec: version, syntax facts,
  statement kinds, operator table, all 53 builtins with arities, the 15 string
  methods, 11 list methods, 9 dict methods, module system and package manager
  rules. Load this first if you need a compact representation.
- `pyhp-qa.jsonl` — 58 chat-format training pairs (system/user/assistant).
  Every code output in the answers was captured by actually executing the
  snippet on the PyHP interpreter — nothing is hallucinated.
- `pyhp-code.jsonl` — 26 instruction → solution pairs for code-generation
  fine-tuning; every solution was parse-checked and executed, with its verified
  output included as `verifiedOutput`.

## Minimal mental model for code generation

- File extension `.pyh`. Statements end with `;`; blocks use braces; comments
  are `//`, `#`, `/* */` (`//` is NOT integer division; `/` is true division).
- Variables: `name = value;` or typed `int x = 5;` (annotations: int, float,
  string, bool, list, dict, var/any — enforced at runtime; float widens int).
- Strings: `"..."` or `'...'`; f-strings: `f"hi {name}, sum={a + b}"`.
- Loops: `while`, `do {...} while`, C-style `for (i = 0; i < n; i++)`,
  `foreach x in xs`, `foreach k, v in xs`. Comprehensions:
  `[x * 2 for x in xs if x > 1]`, `{k: v for k, v in d}`.
- Lambdas: `double = lambda n: n * 2;` (params, colon, single expression).
- Classes: `class Dog extends Animal { function __construct(n) { this.name = n; } }`,
  `super(...)`, `__str__` for string conversion, `isinstance(obj, "Dog")`.
- Errors: `try { throw ValueError("msg"); } catch (ValueError e) { e.message }`
  finally {...}`; classes: Exception, TypeError, ValueError, KeyError,
  IndexError, ZeroDivisionError, MemError, RuntimeError.
- Dot-methods: strings (upper, split, join, find, ...), lists (append, pop,
  sort, ...), dicts (get, has, merge, ...). Callables in dicts are dot-callable.
- Modules: `m = require("./lib.pyh")` or `m = require("pkgname")` → dict of the
  module's top-level functions/lambdas/classes; call as `m.fn(x)`, instantiate
  classes as `m.Class(args)`. Cached per path. Packages: `pyhp pkg add mathx`
  installs into `vendor/`; resolution: ./vendor → $PYHP_REGISTRY → install
  registry (ships `strings`, `mathx`, `texttable`).
- CLI: `pyhp run|build|compile|repl|pkg` (or `php bin/pyhp ...`); script args
  arrive via `argv()`.

## Common pitfalls (verified)

- Dict keys are strings or ints only (no float/bool keys).
- `isinstance(v, "list")` is false for primitives — use `type(v) == "list"`;
  isinstance is for user/error classes.
- `sorted(xs)` has no key parameter yet; write a small selection sort.
- `echo` adds no newline and no separator; `print` adds both (space + newline).
- In compiled mode, `require()` needs a literal string; keep modules stateless.
